page: Amazon Web Services m5ad.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring an AMD EPYC 7571 processor with 8 vCPUs and 4 physical cores. Operating at a clock speed of 2.2 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server includes 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance is built on the Nitro hypervisor and includes 300 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the CPU performance of the AMD EPYC 7571 on this instance is generally limited. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, as well as single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, fall into the bottom 10% of benchmarked servers. However, PassMark CPU and encryption tests achieve average performance, placing in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks register as weak, though the PassMark memory score remains in the average tier.

Database operations and Redis SET performance are positioned in the bottom 25%, indicating potential bottlenecks for high-throughput transactional databases. For machine learning workloads, LLM text generation with a small model performs at an average level, but prompt processing and medium model text generation are poor. Given the inclusion of 300 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside moderate compute capabilities, this instance is suited for general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, and applications requiring temporary local storage rather than high-performance computing or intensive database operations.
